ImageDescription.value:
Map of the routes in the Magruder murders, October 1863, in what was then Idaho Territory (now Idaho and Montana).
  • Lloyd Magruder's party travels from Virginia City (October 3) by way of Beaverhead Rock and Rattlesnake to Bannack, then up Grasshopper Creek, through the Big Hole valley, over Gibbons Pass to Ross's Hole and up the West Fork of the Bitterroot to Nez Perce Pass, and down the Southern Nez Perce Trail to its camp above the Selway River, where five men were killed on the night of October 11.
  • The killers' route: west on the Southern Nez Perce Trail past Magruder Mountain and the Red River to Elk City, past the Mountain House, probably by the northern (Kamiah) branch of the Elk City trail, to a camp on Cottonwood Creek "within about eight miles of the Garrison" (Fort Lapwai), and into Lewiston on October 18.
Solid lines follow a mapped or surveyed historic trail. Dashed lines are approximate, drawn along the valleys and modern roads that follow the old routes. The murder site is shown where the U.S. Forest Service marks it; the exact spot is uncertain. State lines are modern.

Credit.value:
Own work

  • Hydrography: U.S. Geological Survey National Hydrography Dataset (public domain). State lines: U.S. Census Bureau cartographic boundaries 1:500,000 (public domain).
  • Trail alignments:
    • USDA Forest Service Enterprise Data Warehouse trail centerline for Trail 13, "Nez Perce Indian Trail."
    • James G. Huntley, Assessment of the Lewiston–Elk City Trails (Idaho County Historic Preservation Commission), points plotted from General Land Office survey notes.
    • W. W. de Lacy, Map of the Territory of Montana (1865; Library of Congress G4250 1865 .D4).
    • Route corridors drawn along modern roads from OpenStreetMap data (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL) through the waypoints below.
  • Route and waypoints: testimony of William Page, Sacramento Daily Union, February 24, 1864; Idaho State Historical Society, Reference Series No. 285 (1972); H. H. Bancroft, History of Washington, Idaho, and Montana (1890), pp. 241–242; T. J. Dimsdale, The Vigilantes of Montana; N. P. Langford, Vigilante Days and Ways (1890); Ladd Hamilton, This Bloody Deed: The Magruder Incident (Washington State University Press, 1994), pp. 83–84, 230–231.

ImageDescription.value:
Part of the American Views series, this plate depicts the famous Catskill Mountain House. Built in 1823, near Palenville, New York, on a plateau with stunning views of the Hudson Valley on one side and two lakes on the other, this hotel was patronized by the elite in society, including three U.S. presidents Ulysses S. Grant, Chester A. Arthur, and Theodore Roosevelt. The hotel enjoyed a long run of popularity, but eventually closed in 1941. "Cattskill" "Mountain House" "U.S." printed in red with in an oval floral frame topped with an eagle is on the bottom of the plate along with the number "1".

Cattskill Mountain House
